title: Continual Merging Strategy
definition: A strategy for combining LoRAs (Layer-wise Adaptive Quantization) to avoid catastrophic forgetting by merging them sequentially instead of stacking them.

difficulty_levels.beginner: A method for updating a model's abilities over time by combining new parts with the old ones in a way that minimizes forgetting the old knowledge. Instead of adding new parts on top of each other, the new parts are blended with the old ones in a more gradual and organized manner.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: A technique for combining multiple LoRAs (Layer-wise Adaptive Quantization) to minimize catastrophic forgetting. It involves freezing task-specific adapters and adding them compositionally or merging them over time using strategies like orthogonal basis initialization and time-aware scaling.
difficulty_levels.expert: A strategy for combining LoRAs (Layer-wise Adaptive Quantization) that addresses the problem of catastrophic forgetting when merging multiple adapters. It involves merging adapters sequentially, initializing new task learning in an orthogonal subspace, and using time-aware scaling to balance old and new knowledge. This method has been shown to recover much of the performance of the original adapters while significantly reducing storage needs.

extra_fields.insight: By merging adapters sequentially instead of stacking them, we can mitigate the problem of catastrophic forgetting and improve the model's ability to learn and retain knowledge over time.
